unmapped_findings: For the Al-free ternary Fe-30Mn-1.2C reference material, aging leaves the yield strength virtually unchanged relative to the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE), increases hardness slightly, but reduces UTS and TE; embrittlement becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C). No exact numeric YS/UTS/TE values are printed in the text for the specific 500 °C/1 h aged condition, so only these qualitative trends are recorded for this sample.

This sample is the Al-free (x = 0 wt.% Al) reference ternary Fe-30Mn-1.2C composition of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl (wt.%) RAP screening; unlike the 8 wt.% Al variant, no κ-carbide (L′1₂, (Fe,Mn)₃AlC) strengthening is expected upon aging because κ-carbide formation is promoted by Al additions.

The paper presents a temperature-sensitive dislocation-density-based constitutive model for single-phase low-density TWIP (SIMPLEX) steels, the alloy class to which this Fe-30Mn-1.2C sample belongs; however, the model validation shown in Fig. 7 uses a Fe-22wt.%Mn-0.6wt.%C model TWIP alloy, and no sample-specific simulation of Fe-30Mn-1.2C is reported for this sample.
